les: Sewe gelowe, en hoe elkeen fees vier - deel 2
kaps_punt: Feeste en gebruike van 'n verskeidenheid religiee in Suid-Afrika (deel 2 van 2): Afrika-religie, Boeddhisme, Baha'i-geloof.

items.bewering: Sewe van die gelowe wat in Suid-Afrika beoefen word, het elkeen hulle eie feeste.
items.blok: Die dag wanneer 'n gesin die voorouers bedank
items.bron: Religion in South Africa (Wikipedia, citing Census 2022 and the 2013 General Household Survey); GCIS Pocket Guide to South Africa 2004, 'People' chapter: Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Judaism, African traditional religion, Buddhism and the Baha'i faith are all practised in SA, the last two in small numbers. The wording says 'sewe van die gelowe', not 'die sewe gelowe', so it makes no claim that these are the only seven.

items.bewering: In Afrika-religie val die groot dae nie volgens een vaste kalender nie.
items.blok: Die dag wanneer 'n gesin die voorouers bedank
items.bron: UKZN research (ukzn-dspace / researchspace) on imbeleko, which says practice varies from family to family; Wikipedia 'Umkhosi Wokweshwama' (a seasonal first-fruits festival held around the December solstice, not a calendar date); Isolezwe lesiXhosa on harvest thanksgiving held in May in some areas and June in others. The ceremonies are tied to life events and seasons, not to one fixed calendar.

items.bewering: By baie gesinne is daar 'n dag om die voorouers te onthou en te bedank. Die familie en bure kom dan by die huis bymekaar.
items.blok: Die dag wanneer 'n gesin die voorouers bedank
items.bron: The UKZN imbeleko research describes a family ceremony that thanks the ancestors and asks for their protection; Limpopo Provincial Government, 'Ancestors are thanked for good harvest of Marula fruits' (limpopo.gov.za); Isolezwe lesiXhosa on home-brewed thanksgiving beer after the harvest. The quantifier 'baie' is not a claim about everyone.

items.bewering: By baie mense brand daar impepho om die voorouers nader te roep.
items.blok: Die dag wanneer 'n gesin die voorouers bedank
items.bron: Zondi and Ntshangase, Alternation (UKZN), on impepho burned to communicate with the ancestors; IOL report (26 Nov 2012): impepho burnt as a symbol of communicating with ancestors; Markets of Warwick (Durban), Lime and Impepho Market page.

items.bewering: In baie huise praat 'n ouer familielid, dikwels die hoof van die huis, met die voorouers.
items.blok: Die dag wanneer 'n gesin die voorouers bedank
items.bron: Zondi and Ntshangase, Alternation (UKZN): men of particular standing in the family preside at these ceremonies, with women heading households increasingly doing so; the imbeleko sources name the family elder who speaks to the ancestors. 'Dikwels' and 'ouer familielid' match this without restricting it to men, which the sources say is changing.

items.bewering: Daar is kos vir almal wat kom kuier.
items.blok: Die dag wanneer 'n gesin die voorouers bedank
items.bron: Taste.co.za, 'Imbeleko: The meaning of food in the ritual'; the UKZN imbeleko research (an animal is slaughtered and shared); the Limpopo government marula thanksgiving report (the brew is served afterwards).

items.bewering: Afrika-religie is nie een godsdiens met een fees en een gebruik nie. Van plek tot plek en van volk tot volk verskil die gebruike.
items.blok: Nie een fees en een gebruik nie
items.bron: The UKZN imbeleko dissertation notes variation from family to family; the Markets of Warwick page tells Zulu impepho apart from Xhosa (Eastern Cape) impepho; the harvest ceremonies differ between Zulu, Xhosa and Tsonga sources (Isolezwe lesiXhosa, Spencer Museum label, Limpopo government).

items.bewering: Party gesinne hou 'n dag wanneer die familie 'n baba bygekry het.
items.blok: Nie een fees en een gebruik nie
items.bron: UKZN research on imbeleko: a ceremony that introduces a newborn to the ancestors, thanks them and asks them to protect the child; University of Pennsylvania African Languages page on Zulu names (africa.upenn.edu/afl/zulunames.htm).

items.bewering: Ander hou 'n dag nadat die oes ingebring is.
items.blok: Nie een fees en een gebruik nie
items.bron: Isolezwe lesiXhosa: beer brewed at home after the harvest as thanks to the ancestors and Qamata; Spencer Museum of Art (KU), Zulu beer pot label: after the harvest, sorghum beer is made as food for the ancestors; Limpopo Provincial Government on thanking the ancestors for the marula harvest. Note: Umkhosi Wokweshwama is a first-fruits ceremony held at the START of harvest, but the lesson does not name it, and family thanksgiving after the harvest is attested on its own.

items.bewering: Daarom kan niemand sê dat al die mense van hierdie geloof dit eenders doen nie.
items.blok: Nie een fees en een gebruik nie
items.bron: Follows from the variation shown in the sources for the previous items (UKZN; Isolezwe; Limpopo government; Markets of Warwick).

items.bewering: Baie Boeddhiste in Suid-Afrika vier elke jaar 'n fees met die naam Wesak. By die fees onthou hulle die lewe van die Boeddha.
items.bron: Sri Lanka Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 'Vesak Day 2024 Celebrated in South Africa' and 'Vesak Day 2025 Celebrated in South Africa' (mfa.gov.lk), Johannesburg Meditation Centre, Midrand; Wikipedia 'Buddhist holidays' and pluralism.org: Vesak marks the birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha, so 'die lewe van die Boeddha' is a fair summary.

items.bewering: By baie van hulle val dit gewoonlik in Mei op volmaan. Die datum skuif elke jaar, want die fees volg die maan.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Buddhist holidays' / 'Vesak': the full moon of the month Vesakha, usually in May (sometimes April or June); a lunar date, so the Gregorian date moves. reonline.org.uk festivals page: Theravada Vesak usually falls in May. The wording 'by baie van hulle' and 'gewoonlik' covers the April/June years.

items.bewering: Ander Boeddhiste vier die Boeddha se geboortedag op 'n ander dag.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Buddhist holidays'; timeanddate.com 'Buddha's Birthday 2024'; Higashi Honganji USA and the Midwest Buddhist Temple (Chicago): Japan keeps Hanamatsuri on 8 April, Chinese-calendar countries the 8th day of the 4th lunar month, Taiwan the second Sunday of May, and Japanese Mahayana keeps birth, enlightenment and death on separate days.

items.bewering: By die fees gaan baie mense na 'n tempel of na 'n saal toe.
items.bron: Sri Lanka MFA Vesak reports for South Africa (events at the Johannesburg Meditation Centre, Midrand); Wikipedia 'Nan Hua Temple' (Bronkhorstspruit): major festivals are celebrated there.

items.bewering: Die tempel word vir die fees mooi gemaak met blomme en ligte. Mense bring blomme saam en steek 'n kers of wierook op.
items.bron: Sunday Times (Sri Lanka) and Sunday Observer Vesak features: offerings of flowers, incense and lamps, with lanterns and lights as decoration; Sri Lanka MFA 2024/2025 South Africa Vesak reports: an offering of flowers and candles, plus Vesak lanterns and oil lamps at the Midrand event.

items.bewering: Baie Boeddhiste eet by die fees kos sonder vleis.
items.bron: Time Out Sri Lanka and Sunday Times (lk) Vesak features: devotees refrain from meat and alcohol and eat only vegetarian food on the day; Nan Hua Temple (inyourpocket listing) serves vegetarian meals. The quantifier 'baie' is correct, because not all Buddhists are vegetarian.

items.bewering: Party gemeenskappe gee ook kos weg aan mense wat min het.
items.bron: Sunday Observer / The Morning (lk) on dana (giving) at Vesak: dansalas giving away food and drink, and giving to the poor.

items.bewering: Die Baha'i-geloof se eerste dag van die jaar is 'n fees met die naam Naw-Ruz.
items.bron: USC Office of Religious and Spiritual Life, Baha'i Holy Days calendar; Religion Media Centre factsheet 'Baha'i New Year'; Tanenbaum 2026 Naw-Ruz Fact Sheet: Naw-Ruz is the Baha'i New Year, the first day of the Badi year.

items.bewering: Naw-Ruz val elke jaar om en by 21 Maart.
items.bron: USC Baha'i Holy Days calendar: 21 March 2027, 20 March 2028, 20 March 2029, fixed to the vernal equinox. 'Om en by' correctly covers the 20/21 March variation. Rekord (Citizen), 20 March 2019: Tshwane Baha'is celebrate on 21 March.

items.bewering: In die dae voor die fees eet en drink baie volwassenes bedags niks nie.
items.bron: USC Baha'i Holy Days calendar and the Tanenbaum Naw-Ruz Fact Sheet: a 19-day fast in early March in which adult Baha'is in good health go without food and drink from sunrise to sunset, with exemptions. 'Baie volwassenes' matches the exemptions.

items.bewering: Die fees begin die aand wanneer die son ondergaan. Dan eet mense weer saam, en die nuwe jaar begin.
items.bron: USC Baha'i Holy Days calendar: Baha'i days begin at sunset, so the holy day begins the evening before; the fast ends the day before Naw-Ruz. Washtenaw County Baha'i Center Naw-Ruz listings: a meal to break the fast together. Bahai.org news 'Baha'is celebrate new year' (after sundown on the eve).

items.bewering: Baha'i-gemeenskappe kom in 'n sentrum of by iemand se huis bymekaar.
items.bron: Bahá'ís of Canada news ('Baha'is celebrate Naw-Ruz with friends and neighbours'): community celebrations in centres and homes; Washtenaw County Baha'i Center Naw-Ruz celebrations; Rekord (Citizen) 2019 on Tshwane community celebrations.

items.bewering: Mense trek mooi aan en bring kos saam vir die tafel.
items.bron: Bahaiteachings.org 'Manifold meanings of the Baha'i New Year' and religionfacts.com 'Naw-Ruz': new or freshly cleaned clothes are worn. Washtenaw County Baha'i Center and Naperville Baha'i Community listings, and Bahá'ís of Canada (Sidney, B.C.): potluck meals are a common feature of community celebrations.

items.bewering: By baie vieringe lees iemand gebede voor, en daar is dikwels ook musiek.
items.bron: Memorial University of Newfoundland, Local Religions, 'Naw-Ruz, 167 BE': a feast followed by prayers, readings, music and social time; Bahá'ís of Canada: celebrations often feature music, feasting, dancing and prayer.

items.bewering: Baie mense bly daardie dag van die werk en van die skool af.
items.bron: USC Baha'i Holy Days calendar: Naw-Ruz is one of the nine Baha'i holy days on which work is suspended, and school attendance is suspended too. 'Baie mense' is correctly not 'almal', because it is not a public holiday in SA (it coincides with Human Rights Day, 21 March, in some years: Rekord 2019).

items.bewering: Party gemeenskappe nooi ook vriende en bure van ander gelowe saam.
items.bron: Bahá'ís of Canada, 'Baha'is celebrate Naw-Ruz with friends and neighbours': holy days are open to everyone; Ipoh Echo (Malaysia) 2018: friends from other faiths are invited to join the celebration.

items.bewering: Die drie feeste in hierdie les verskil van mekaar, en tog kom drie dinge by elkeen voor. Mense kom bymekaar ... By elke fees is daar kos. By elke fees is daar ook iets wat die mense saam vier.
items.bron: The comparison was tested as a set against the sources above. Gathering: the family and neighbours (ATR sources), temple or hall (MFA Vesak reports), centre or home (Bahá'ís of Canada). Food: imbeleko and thanksgiving food (Taste.co.za, Limpopo government), vegetarian food and dana (Sunday Times lk), the meal that breaks the fast (USC, Washtenaw). Something celebrated together: in each case. The mapping holds for all three, and the closing sentence keeps the difference between them, so a learner is not led to think the three are one festival under different names.

items.bewering: Mense van al sewe hierdie gelowe woon in hierdie land langs mekaar. In een straat kan bure in een jaar drie verskillende feeste vier.
items.bron: Religion in South Africa (Wikipedia, Census 2022); GCIS Pocket Guide 2004: all seven are present in SA, so neighbours of different faiths is a real possibility ('kan', not 'doen').

items.bewering: Jy hoef nie dieselfde te glo om by iemand anders se fees te kuier nie.
items.bron: Bahá'ís of Canada: Baha'i holy days are open to everyone; Sri Lanka MFA 2025 report: the Midrand Vesak event was multireligious, with leaders of several faiths taking part. The ATR block itself places neighbours at the family gathering. As a general 'hoef nie' statement it is supported; it does not claim every ceremony is open to everyone.

items.bewering: fees: 'n Dag of 'n tyd wat mense saam onthou en saam vier.
items.bron: Accurate as a plain-language gloss, and consistent with the three festivals as documented above (Vesak commemorates the Buddha's life, Naw-Ruz marks the new year, the ATR thanksgiving days remember the ancestors). Dictionary sense: a celebration or festive occasion.

items.bewering: gebruik: Iets wat 'n groep mense oor en oor op dieselfde manier doen.
items.bron: Accurate gloss of 'gebruik' in the sense of custom or practice (a usual, repeated way of doing something shared by a group); consistent with how the sources above describe imbeleko, the Vesak offerings and the Naw-Ruz meal.

items.bewering: voorouers: Die mense in jou familie van wie jy afstam en wat reeds oorlede is, soos 'n ouma of oupa wat al gesterf het.
items.bron: The general sense of 'voorouer' (forebear, a person one is descended from); in the ATR sense used here the ancestors are deceased family members (GCIS Pocket Guide 2004: ancestors are of great significance; UKZN imbeleko research: the family's ancestors are addressed). The example, a grandparent who has died, is correct.

items.bewering: impepho: 'n Geurige plant wat mense brand om hul voorouers nader te roep en met hulle te praat.
items.bron: Markets of Warwick (Durban): the yellow-flowered impepho plant used by Zulu people, sold for burning; Zondi and Ntshangase, Alternation (UKZN), and IOL 2012: burned to communicate with the ancestors.

items.bewering: wierook: Iets wat mense brand omdat die rook lekker ruik, dikwels by gebede of in 'n tempel.
items.bron: Sunday Times (lk) Vesak feature: incense offered in the temple, its scent standing for the Buddha's virtues. A substance burned for its fragrant smoke, often in worship, is the standard sense of incense. The gloss is simplified but not false.

items.bewering: Wesak: Die fees waarop baie Boeddhiste die lewe van die Boeddha onthou.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Buddhist holidays' / 'Vesak'; pluralism.org 'Buddha's Birthday': it commemorates the birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha. 'Baie' agrees with the study block's note that other Buddhists use other days.

items.bewering: Naw-Ruz: Die fees op die eerste dag van die Baha'i-jaar.
items.bron: USC Baha'i Holy Days calendar; Religion Media Centre factsheet 'Baha'i New Year'; Tanenbaum 2026 Naw-Ruz Fact Sheet.

opsomming: Every checkable claim in all fifteen blocks (eight study blocks and seven glossary entries) was checked afresh against outside sources. Nothing is false or unsettled: the quantifiers ('baie', 'party', 'gewoonlik', 'om en by 21 Maart') are well judged throughout, the two 'eerste dag' superlatives about Naw-Ruz hold, and the comparison of the three festivals holds as a set.
